lawyer:
Md. Nurul Huq with A B.M. Khairul Huq, Md. Mahabub Alam ----- For the Petitioner. 
Abdur Rab-II ----- For the Opposite Party
parties:
M/S Subarna Trading Co. Ltd ----- Petitioner
Vs.
M/S Overseas Traders ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This rule is directed against the judgment and order passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Dacca dated 20.12.79 in Misc. Appeal No. 306 of 1979 affirming these dated 30.7.79 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court Dacca, in Misc. Case No. 273 of 1978 arising out of Title Suit No. 140 of that Court. 

 2. The opposite party as plaintiff filed the suit against the petitioner for ejectment. The petitioner filed written statement and contested the suit. During the pendency of the suit the petitioner on 23.1.78 prayed for adjournment of the case and the court fixed 20.3.78 for the hearing of the suit. There-after he engaged Mr. Md. Nurul Huq senior Advocate of this court for conducting the suit. Mr. Nurul Huq on that date was engaged in the High Court Division and as such an application for adjournment of the case on that ground was filed before that court. The learned Subordinate Judge rejected the prayer another application was filed by the petitioner after the rejection of his first application for reconsideration of the previous order but that was also rejected and the suit was decreed ex-parte. As against the said ex-parte decree the petitioner filed an application under Order 9, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for the restoration of the suit to file. It was contended in that application that the petitioner appointed a Senior Advocate for conducting his case but as he was heavily engaged on the date fixed i.e. 20.3.78 in the High Court Division an application for adjournment was filed but unfortunately the Court did not grant time, rejected the two applications filed by the defendant petitioner and decreed the suit ex-parte. The plaintiff opposite party contested the application contending, inter alia that the petitioner was not diligent in conducting the suit and his intention was to drag the same and as such the court was right in rejecting the applications for adjournment and decreeing the suit ex-parte. The learned Subordinate Judge rejected the application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure holding that on the date when the learned Senior Advocate was engaged, the petitioner knew that the learned Senior Advocate will not be able to appear on that date and as such the petitioner ought to have made alternative arrangement in view of the fact that the case was fixed for that date. The application for adjournment was filed on behalf of Mr. Nurul Huq who was engaged in the case and the clerk of Mr. Nurul Huq deposed in the case to the effect that Mr. Nurul Huq was engaged in a part heard matter and in moving a motion in the High Court Division. He had also produced a cause list of the High Court Division to prove the assertion and the motion to prove that he was engaged on that date. In spite of that the learned Subordinate Judge held that 20.3.78 was fixed for hearing and another lawyer was conducting the suit but he was not instructed to conduct the suit on the date. He further held that the petitioner took the previous order of the court very lightly though he had the opportunity to be ready for hearing of the suit on that date. He also found that it was known to the petitioner that the learned Advocate who has been subsequently engaged will not able to appear on the date fixed and as such he ought to have made alternative arrangement. He held that the pre-occupation of the learned Advocate subsequently engaged cannot be a ground for restoration under Order 9 rule 13 C.P.C. As against the said judgment and order the petitioner preferred an appeal. 

 3. The learned Additional District Judge affirmed the Judgment and order of the learned Subordinate Judge He also held that the engagement of Mr. Nurul Huq, the learned Advocate who was a heavily engaged lawyer in the High Court Division in the case was nothing but a device to drag the suit and not to finish it despite the time passed earlier. So he also found that the engagement of the learned Advocate Mr. Nurul Huq and his inability to appear on 20 3.78 cannot be a ground for getting relief under Order 9, rule 13 C.P.C. As against the said order of the learned Additional District Judge the petitioner moved a revisional application before this Hon'ble Court on 7.1.80 and the learned Judge without issuing any rule set aside the order of the Courts below and restored the suit to file on the defendant petitioner's paying an adjournment cost of Tk. 400/- to the opposite party within two weeks from that date and the said adjournment cost was made condition precedent to the restoration of the suit to file. As against that order of the learned Judge of the High Court Division the plaintiff. filed an appeal before the Appellate Division and the Appellate Division allowed the appeal and sent the case hack to this court for coming to a decision after hearing both the parties in view of the fact that the order passed by the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division was violative of the principles of natural justice. 

 4. Mr. Nurul Huq, the learned Advocate appeared on behalf of the defendant petitioner and Mr. Abdur Rab-II appeared on behalf of the plaintiff opposite party. Mr. Nurul Huq, the learned Advocate submits that pursuant to the order of the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division date 7.1.80 he has deposited the costs awarded within the time granted by this Court. He also submits that the defendant engaged him for appearing and contesting the case but unfortunately for him and for his client, he could not appear on that date in view of his pre-occupation in the High Court Division. He submits that the application filed by the learned Advocate for adjournment was bonafide and in good faith on the ground of his pre-occupation in the High Court and he expected that a short adjournment will be granted. But the judgment of the learned Sub-ordinate Judge shows that he took exception to this prayer for adjournment in view of the fact that the previous adjournments were granted by the Court on the prayer of the defendant and he has found that absence of the Advocate for the petitioner cannot be a sufficient cause for restoring the case. The learned Additional District Judge has also, according to him, committed the same mistake. The Courts below have taken exception to the fact that Mr. Nurul Huq was engaged by the petitioner knowing fully well of his engagement in some other court and this cannot be taken as sufficient ground. He contended that the Court of appeal below has erred in holding that the petitioner ought to have engaged some other Senior Advocate to instruct his junior Advocate to contest the suit. His finding that the engagement of the Senior Advocate in a premeditated act only to protract the suit to the harassment of the other party is based on surmises and conjectures. Mr. Abdur Rab II. the learned Advocate, on the other hand,. submits that the Courts below have found as fact that there was no sufficient ground for the absence of the defendant on that date and in view of the findings arrived at by the Courts below this Court has no jurisdiction to entertain this application under section 115 C.P.C. in support of his contention he has relied upon some decisions of the Appellate Division such as 28 D.L.R. (A.D) 57, 29 D.L.R.(A.D) 28 and 31 D.L.R. (A.D. 123 and A.I.R. 1937,1 Allahabad, 691. There cannot be any other view as to the contention that the High Court Division cannot in exercise of jurisdiction under section 115 C.P.C. alter the findings of facts but the facts and drum stances of the present ones are, completely different and it cannot be said in the context of the present case that the High Court Division in revision cannot interfere with the decision of the Courts below. In this matter the question is whether sufficient cause has been made out by the petitioner in his application under Order 9 rule 13 C.P.C. Both the courts below have considered that when a date was fixed for peremptory hearing the party while engaging an Advocate must see as to whether he is available on the date or not since the learned Advocate has stated that he will be engaged on that date the party should have engaged another Advocate or should have instructed his previous Advocate to conduct the case. So the question before the Court is whether sufficient cause has been made out from the facts produced before court. Both the courts below have come to the conclusion that there was lack of diligence on the part of the petitioner in view of the fact that the petitioner knew fully well that the lawyer engaged will not be able to appear on the date fixed and in spite of that he engaged him. It is from the fact that the learned Advocate was engaged on that date, it cannot be said that there was lack of diligence on the part of the defendant petitioner. The defendant petitioner has engaged the learned Advocate and the learned Advocate has filed an application for adjournment on the ground of his being engaged in the High Court Division. It is curious enough that the learned Additional District Judge while disposing of the matter did not state the fact that the learned Advocate was engaged in the High Court Division. He has only noted about it as the learned Advocate's pre-occupation in some other court. In spite of having known the fact that the application stated about the learned Advocate's pre-occupation in the High Court Division the learned Additional District Judge while disposing of the Misc. Appeal has stated that the learned Advocate was engaged in some other court. While mentioning about the superior courts, the subordinate Courts should not mention in such a manner. This attitude of the learned Additional District Court is highly deprecated and is noted with disapproval. In view of the fact that the petitioner could not have his case represented in view of the engagement of the learned Advocate engaged by him, the interest of justice demands that the petitioner should be given a chance for the rehearing of the case on terms or else the petitioner would suffer irreparable loss for no fault of his only in engaging a Senior Advocate of this court to argue his case. This engagement of the Sensor Advocate has gone against him. It is, therefore, ordered that the orders of the Courts below are set aside on condition of the defendant petitioner's paying to the opposite party an amount of Tk. 400/- irrespective of the result of the suit. As noted earlier the said amount has been already set in Court pursuant to a previous order of this Court which may be withdrawn by the plaintiff. 

 5. The result, therefore, is that this rule is made absolute on condition of payment of Tk. 400/- to plaintiff opposite party which the plaintiff opposite party will be at liberty to withdraw irrespective of the result of the case. In the facts and circumstances, however, there will be no order as to costs. Let the suit be disposed of within one month of the receipt of order of this Court. The hearing of the suit must be fixed after intimation of the arrival of the records to the parties.
